principal.definition: Local Aso-4 fallout thickness in cm. Four point estimates use the logged depth spans of Aso-4 layers in Ulleung Basin cores. Three geological minima enter the fitting input at their thresholds and the upper limit stays one-sided.

primary_source.citation: Chun, J.-H., Ikehara, K. and Han, S.-J. (2004). Evidence in Ulleung Basin Sediment Cores for a Termination II (Penultimate Deglaciation) Eruption of the Aso-3 Tephra. The Quaternary Research 43, 99–112.
primary_source.fields: Table 1, printed p. 102, gives station coordinates, water depths and paired stratigraphic depths below the core top. The Fig. 2 legend distinguishes tephra (TP) from mud facies. Fig. 4c photographs the named layer in 95PC-6. Fig. 5a shows a shard, and Table 2 and Figs. 6–7 concern selected samples. The chemistry depths are separate from the paired depths.

interpretation: The authors log a named tephra layer at each core. Table 1 reports its stratigraphic position as a pair of depths rather than a separate thickness field. The paired depths, lithofacies log and distinct assay depths support interpreting each difference as a recovered layer span. Only 95PC-6 has an Aso-4 core photograph in the 2004 paper. The other three have no described pair of sharp contacts. Ash fraction and primary uncompacted thickness remain unresolved in all four. The separate Aso-3 column is excluded. Table 1 marks Aso-3 at 96EBP-7 as na (not acquired). Longitude 131°12.3′ N is printed in that row. Fig. 1 places the station east of Greenwich. Coordinates are converted from decimal arcminutes with 0.1 arcminute source precision and no datum shift.
selection: Four interpreted layer spans enter as point thicknesses with a basis and evidence qualifier on each input row. No station ID match was found in the preceding accepted or excluded records. The ledger gives nearest earlier accepted and S2 presence-only coordinates using WGS84 geodesics. Six prior pseudo rows remain outside the fit.
preservation: The source attributes Aso ash to airborne co-ignimbrite dispersal. Three sites are near a submarine channel and the fourth is on the flat basin floor. Currents, bioturbation, sediment focusing and compaction can change local marine thickness. The paper gives no numerical restoration or site-specific diagnosis of secondary emplacement of these four Aso-4 beds.

related_records.use: The author reproduces the 2004 photograph. It documents the same 95PC-6 layer.

related_records.citation: Chun et al. (1998), J. Geol. Soc. Korea 34, 192–210
related_records.use: The institutional record identifies the earlier survey and supplies no full text. No contact readings or replicate measurements are taken from this record.
